text: Compare ROSE with TQUG: R, position 18, to T, position 20 is +2. O, position 15, to Q, position 17 is +2. S, position 19, to U, position 21 is +2. E, position 5, to G, position 7 is +2. The rule is: move each letter two steps forward. Apply it to LILY. L becomes N, I becomes K, and the second L becomes N. Now the last letter, Y. Its position is 25, and 25 + 2 = 27. That is beyond Z, so subtract 26 to get position 1, which is A. LILY is coded as NKNA. If you wrote something odd for the last letter, you've just met the wrap-around trap. It's better to meet it here than in the exam.
